steps.title: Reveal Heroes
text: Each player places their hero card face-up in their hero zone.
Your hero determines your class, talents, life total, and intellect (cards drawn at end of turn).

steps.title: Determine First Player
text: Randomly pick a player, who then decides who goes first.
For the first game of a match, use any mutually agreeable random method. For subsequent games, the loser of the previous game decides.

steps.title: Choose Equipment & Weapons
text: Secretly select your starting arena-cards from your card-pool.
Choose up to one card per equipment zone (Arms, Chest, Head, Legs) and weapon zone(s). Place them face-down in their zones or in a single face-down pile.
Your choice stays hidden until the game begins.

steps.title: Shuffle & Cut
text: Shuffle your deck and present it to your opponent to shuffle or cut.
After your opponent cuts, place your deck in its zone. You may no longer change which cards you selected.

steps.title: Reveal & Draw
text: Reveal your weapons and equipment. Draw cards up to your hero's intellect.
Starting with the first player, each player reveals their equipment and weapons face-up. Then each draws cards equal to their hero's intellect.
The first player begins their first turn.

steps.title: Match Format
text: 55-minute rounds, best of 1.
Classic Constructed tournaments use best-of-1 matches with 55-minute rounds. If time expires, the turn player finishes their turn plus one additional turn. If still no winner, the game is a draw.

steps.title: Match Format
text: 35-minute rounds, best of 1.
Silver Age tournaments use best-of-1 matches with 35-minute rounds. If time expires, the turn player finishes their turn plus one additional turn. If still no winner, the game is a draw.

steps.title: Deck — Card Pool & Deck
text: Card pool: exactly 80 cards. Select at least 60 cards from your pool to form your deck.

steps.title: Deck — Hero & Restrictions
text: Must use a non-young (adult) hero.
Up to 3 copies of each unique card (same name AND color).
Cards must match your hero's class and talents — generic cards can go in any deck.

steps.title: Deck — Card Pool & Deck
text: Card pool: exactly 55 cards. Select exactly 40 cards from your pool to form your deck.

steps.title: Deck — Hero & Restrictions
text: Must use a young hero.
All cards must be common, rare, or basic rarity.
Up to 2 copies of each unique card (same name AND color).
Cards must match your hero's class and talents — generic cards can go in any deck.

steps.title: Deck — Equipment
text: Up to 1 card per equipment zone (Arms, Chest, Head, Legs) and weapon zone(s).
Unused pool cards become your inventory for sideboarding between games.

steps.title: Play Area Layout
text: Flesh and Blood uses a distinct play area with several zones:
bullets: **Hero zone** — Your hero card sits here, face-up. It shows your life total, class, talents, and intellect.
**Weapon zones** — You may have 1 or 2 weapon zones. Weapons are equipped here face-up and can be used to attack.
**Equipment zones** — Arms, Chest, Head, and Legs. Equipment is equipped here face-up and provides passive effects or defense.
**Deck zone** — Your draw pile. Cards enter your hand from here.
**Graveyard** — Defeated equipment, used action cards, and discarded cards go here face-up.
**Banished zone** — Cards removed from the game go here face-up. Some effects let you play cards from banish.
**Pitch zone** — When you pitch a card, it goes here temporarily. At the end of the turn, all pitched cards go to the bottom of your deck.
**Arsenal** — One face-down card you can play as though it were in your hand. Only one card at a time.
**Combat chain** — When you attack, the attack card and any defending/reaction cards form a temporary chain link here.

steps.title: Pitching
text: Instead of using lands or mana, FaB uses a pitching system. Each card has a pitch value (1, 2, or 3 colored pips in the top-left). To gain resources, discard a card from your hand — you gain resource points equal to its pitch value. You can pitch multiple cards in a turn to pay for expensive plays.

steps.title: The Combat Chain
text: When you attack, the combat chain opens. Attacking cards form chain links. The defending player may defend with cards from hand or equipment. Both players can play attack/defense reactions. Each chain link resolves in order: Declare attack → Declare defense → Reactions → Damage.

steps.title: Defense Values
text: Every card has a defense value (bottom-right number). When defending, you block damage equal to the card's defense value. Equipment has defense too, but may take durability loss.
